Avocado Night Cream Original vs Fake: How to Check Before You Buy

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 16 October 2026Updated 16 October 20267 min read
Quick answer

An original avocado night cream comes sealed, with a batch number, mfg and expiry dates, full ingredient list, manufacturer address, MRP and licence details on the label. Buy from the brand's site or official marketplace store, and avoid jars with no label details, very low prices or promises of big changes in days.

  • Check for an inner seal, batch number, and printed mfg and expiry dates.
  • A real label shows the ingredients, manufacturer address, MRP and licence details.
  • Very low prices, refilled jars and quick-change promises are red flags.
  • Mirc Glow buyers can send a batch number photo on WhatsApp +91 99808 81230 to check a jar.

To check if your avocado night cream is original, look at the jar and the seller before you open it. An original jar is sealed, has a batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, a full ingredient list, the manufacturer's name and address, the MRP and the licence details printed on the label, and it comes from the brand's own website or its official marketplace store.

Searching "avocado night cream original" makes sense: copies are common because the cream is popular in India. This guide shows you what a real label looks like, the red flags that point to a fake, and how to check a Mirc Glow jar in a few minutes.

Why fake avocado night creams are a problem

A fake jar is not just a waste of money. Nobody knows who filled it, what is inside, how old it is or how it was stored. Some unregulated creams sold loose or through random pages may contain ingredients that should never be in an everyday face cream, which is why a quick, dramatic change on the skin is a warning sign, not a good sign.

We cover the hidden ingredients and the risks in detail in our guide on how to spot fake avocado whitening creams. Here we focus on the checks you can do at home before you use a single drop.

How to check an avocado night cream original: 8 label checks

Hold the jar or box in good light and check each point.

  1. Sealed jar. The outer box or shrink wrap should be intact, and the jar should have an inner seal or foil under the lid. A jar that opens straight to the cream, with finger marks or a dented surface, may have been opened or refilled.
  2. Batch number. Look for "Batch No." or "B. No." printed clearly. It should match on the box and the jar if both carry it.
  3. Manufacturing and expiry dates. Both should be printed, not handwritten, and the expiry should be well in the future.
  4. Full ingredient list. Not just "avocado extract". A real cosmetic lists its ingredients, usually in order from most to least.
  5. Manufacturer name and address. A proper company name and a full address, not just a phone number or a social media handle.
  6. MRP printed. Indian rules require the maximum retail price on the pack. A sticker that covers or changes it is a reason to ask questions.
  7. Licence details. Cosmetics made in India normally show the manufacturing licence number on the label. A pack with no licence line at all is a red flag.
  8. Net weight. The weight in grams should be printed and should match what the listing says.

Check the cream itself: colour, smell and texture

Once the seal is broken, look and smell before you apply.

  • Colour. It should look even all through the jar, with no streaks, dark spots or a watery layer on top.
  • Smell. It should smell the same every time you buy it. A sour, rancid or chemical smell suggests an old or badly stored product.
  • Texture. Smooth and consistent. Grainy, split or very runny cream is a reason to stop and contact the seller.

Even with an original jar, do a patch test behind the ear or on the inner arm for 24 to 48 hours before using it on your face.

Red flags that point to a fake

Original jarRed flag
Sealed box and inner sealNo seal, loose lid, or a refilled-looking jar
Batch number, mfg and expiry dates printedMissing dates, or dates on a handwritten sticker
Full ingredient list and manufacturer addressNo label details at all, or only a phone number
MRP printed on the packNo MRP, or a price far below the brand's own price
Cosmetic wording such as "more even-looking"Ads promising "whitening in 4 days" or "in 7 days"
Sold by the brand or its official storeLoose cream sold in branded-looking jars, or unknown resellers

A very low price is one of the clearest signs. If a jar is selling for a fraction of the price on the brand's own site, ask why.

Where to buy an original avocado night cream

The safest place is always the brand itself, or the brand's official store on a marketplace. Be careful with unknown resellers, roadside stalls, and pages that sell "branded" cream from big tubs into small jars.

After you buy: use it the right way

An original cream still needs to be used well. Take a pea-sized amount at night on clean skin, and wear sunscreen every morning, because kojic acid makes daily sun protection important. Skin usually feels softer within the first few nights. A more even-looking tone takes 8 to 12 weeks of regular use with sunscreen, because skin renews roughly every 4 to 6 weeks.

Stop using any cream that stings, burns or causes a rash, and see a dermatologist if it does not settle, or if you are pregnant or have melasma or painful acne.

Short answers

How do I know if my avocado night cream is original? Check for a sealed jar, a printed batch number, mfg and expiry dates, a full ingredient list, the manufacturer's address, MRP and licence details. Then confirm you bought it from the brand or its official store.

Is a very cheap avocado night cream fake? Not always, but a price far below the brand's own price is a strong warning sign. Ask the seller for label photos before you buy.

Can an original cream show results in 7 days? Skin can feel softer in a few nights, but a more even-looking tone takes 8 to 12 weeks with sunscreen. Promises of big changes in days are a red flag.
